groups.name: Probability components and signed reconstruction
groups.domain: All 2x2 half-grid matrices P with nonnegative P and I-P; exact idempotence. Haar decomposition on nine rational priors and an invertible signed-coordinate change.

groups.name: Least simultaneous prediction and update closure
groups.domain: All deterministic one-action maps through three states; every initial partition with at least two blocks; likelihood entries 1/4,1/2,3/4 with complementary report. All half-grid 3-state Markov rows for one fixed likelihood/partition. Independent enumeration of every refining partition.

groups.name: Joint instrument, exact filtering, and feedback
groups.domain: Every deterministic instrument on three states with two reports and partition (0,0,1), compared with all deterministic coarse instruments. Exact rational 8-to-4 sensor filtering for all binary feedback trees through horizon three and selected point/midpoint priors. Correlated-marginal and malformed-kernel controls.

groups.name: Whole path error and sharp conditional amplification
groups.domain: All pairs of 4-cell quarter-grid probability laws and all nonempty events. Binary controlled sensors with three exact accuracies, three initial beliefs, every horizon-two binary feedback tree; full path total variation and its state/report projections. Same-policy failure control.

groups.name: Exact compressed belief decisions and policy enumeration
groups.domain: 8-to-4 sensor beliefs with 3 exact observation accuracies, 4 charges, point/midpoint priors and horizons 0..3. Direct enumeration of all 1,446 depth-three binary-observation trees for the calibrated diagonal prior. Exact expected stopping cost and number of reports.

groups.name: Uniform model comparison before optimizing policies
groups.domain: All 38 depth-two binary-calibration trees, observation accuracies 1/2, 3/4, 1 and prior target masses 1/4,1/2,3/4. Paired fixed-tree and optimum regret comparisons at cost 1/20. Three-report exact sensitivity at true accuracy 37/50.

limits: Six bounded domains, not six universal computational proofs.
No learning, sampling, external interaction or proof kernel.
